newsitem.title: UK: Commonwealth delays action on Nigeria.
newsitem.headline: Commonwealth delays action on Nigeria.

text.p: Commonwealth foreign ministers have delayed taking action against Nigeria, which has been suspended from the group because of the military government's execution of dissidents.

The Commonwealth Ministerial Action Group (CMAG) ended a two-day meeting in London on Tuesday saying it was inviting more information from "all interested parties," before writing up a report for October's Commonwealth summit in Edinburgh.

The group "reiterated its concern that all political detainees, including Chief Moshood Abiola had not been released and that detention without trial was still taking place in Nigeria," CMAG said in a statement.
Abiola is widely assumed to have won Nigeria's 1993 presidential election which was annulled in mid-count by military rulers who had promised the vote would return the country to civilian rule.
The statement also noted, without comment, that local government elections had been delayed for three months.
Britain's opposition Labour Party protested at the Commonwealth's inaction.

"CMAG has reached an impasse over Nigeria. I fear that it is paving the way for a sell-out. The only people who will take comfort from this are the military junta in Nigeria," Labour's shadow foreign minister Tony Lloyd said in a statement.
Nigeria was suspended from Commonwealth membership in 1995 after it executed writer Ken Saro Wiwa and eight other activists.
